note: Maps X12 Claim Adjustment Reason Codes (CARC) and common consumer-letter phrases to one of six appeal types. Consumer denial letters usually paraphrase rather than print the code; match phrases first, codes second. If more than one type matches, prefer in this order: medical_necessity, prior_auth, out_of_network, not_covered, administrative, timely_filing. If nothing matches, appeal_type = unknown and the app asks the user one question: 'What reason does the letter give?' with the six plain-English choices. Code meanings are from the X12 CARC list; verify wording against x12.org/codes/claim-adjustment-reason-codes before launch.

appeal_types.plain: Denied for missing or wrong information

carc_meanings.16: Claim lacks information or has billing errors
carc_meanings.4: Procedure code inconsistent with modifier or modifier missing
carc_meanings.31: Patient cannot be identified as our insured
carc_meanings.22: May be covered by another payer (coordination of benefits)
carc_meanings.58: Treatment rendered in an inappropriate place of service

phrases: not eligible on date of service
appeal_types.who_fixes_it: Usually the provider's billing office (resubmit a corrected claim). The patient's letter asks the plan to reprocess and copies the provider.
appeal_types.what_wins: Supply the missing item or the corrected code; ask for reprocessing rather than a formal appeal where the plan allows it.

appeal_types.plain: Denied because the claim was filed late

carc_meanings.29: The time limit for filing has expired

appeal_types.who_fixes_it: The provider. In-network providers generally cannot bill the patient for their own late filing; the letter says so and asks the provider to write off or prove timely submission.
appeal_types.what_wins: Proof of timely original submission (clearinghouse report), or the provider's contract barring balance billing.

appeal_types.plain: Denied because approval wasn't obtained first

carc_meanings.15: Authorization number missing, invalid, or does not apply
carc_meanings.62: Payment denied for absence of, or exceeded, pre-certification/authorization

appeal_types.who_fixes_it: Patient and provider together. Emergencies never require prior authorization; the letter leads with that when the service was emergency care.
appeal_types.what_wins: Emergency exception; retroactive authorization request; showing the provider was responsible for obtaining it; the plan's own failure to respond to a timely request.

appeal_types.plain: Denied as not a covered benefit

carc_meanings.204: Service not covered under the patient's current benefit plan
carc_meanings.119: Benefit maximum for this period has been reached
carc_meanings.109: Claim not covered by this payer; send to correct payer
carc_meanings.151: Payment adjusted because the frequency exceeds plan limits
carc_meanings.55: Procedure deemed experimental or investigational by the payer

appeal_types.who_fixes_it: Patient. The fight is over the plan document's words.
appeal_types.what_wins: Quoting the plan's own coverage language; showing the service fits a different covered category; for 'experimental', showing FDA approval or standard-of-care guidelines (needs the doctor).

carc_meanings.50: Non-covered service because it is not deemed a medical necessity by the payer
carc_meanings.56: Procedure has not been deemed proven to be effective by the payer

appeal_types.who_fixes_it: Patient with the treating doctor. The patient files; the doctor supplies the letter of medical necessity and records.
appeal_types.what_wins: A letter of medical necessity that answers the plan's stated criteria point by point, the relevant records, and the plan's own clinical policy quoted back. Ask for a peer-to-peer review between the doctor and the plan's reviewer.

appeal_types.plain: Denied or paid less because the provider was out of network

carc_meanings.242: Services not provided by network/primary care providers
carc_meanings.243: Services not authorized by network/primary care providers
carc_meanings.38: Services not provided or authorized by designated (network/primary care) providers

appeal_types.who_fixes_it: Patient. Federal No Surprises Act protections apply to emergency care and to out-of-network clinicians at an in-network facility.
appeal_types.what_wins: No Surprises Act (emergency; ancillary providers at an in-network facility; air ambulance); network adequacy (no in-network provider available in time or distance); continuity of care.

urgent_flags.note: If any of these appear, the verdict leads with the expedited (72-hour) appeal and a 'call your plan today' line, before anything else.
